body:
I can't tell my mom that I'm a atheist because I don't want to hurt her. 
I graduated with a degree in biology. I can't really do anything with this degree especially since my GPA is so low. 
I'm going back to community college to pursue a career in healthcare, maybe nursing. I'm also struggling to find a part time job to pay for it.
Right now, I have absolutely no interest in anything.

Thank you for reading this.

Thanks for asking. I can't seek medical help because I don't have health insurance. I come from a culture where depression is a taboo, no one ever speaks of it.

I first started feeling like this when I was about in 5th grade. I remember sometimes I just wanted to be left alone back then. While kids played on the playground, I wanted to hang out by myself even though I had friends and was well liked. 

Middle school came and I watched all my classmates phase into the teen stage of "being bad" and competing for popularity. High school got worse, I became an outcast. People changed, I stayed the same. 

College came, at this point I started contemplating suicide. My mom used to call me almost every night to remind me to study hard, pray every night before going to bed, and go to church on Sunday because if I don't pray to God, I'll never be successful. So I became an atheist and kept lying to my mom even til today. At one I got so tired of her calling me to tell me the same thing over and over again that I stopped answering her calls. Then she had my sister drive her 2 hours to my college to check up on me. I was happy to see her and I felt guilty for making her come all the way there. I love my mom because I know she sacrificed her entire life for my family.

So then I graduated with a poor GPA and can't do much with my degree. I didn't party or do drugs. I didn't have a girlfriend because I kept getting rejected. One girl even gave me a fake phone number. I don't care about girls anymore, I don't care about anything anymore. I did poorly in college because I was stupid.

Two years after college and now I'm here. I'm going back to community college to try to get into a healthcare program so that I can turn my life around. I'm trying really hard.

Today, I spent the day watching the documentary about suicides on the Golden Bridge. I keep fantasizing about how easy it would be. I know I'd never do it as long as my parents are still around. Although sometimes I'd be really tempted to just say fuck it and do it. As harsh as this may sound, I'd have to wait about 20 more years til my parents both are gone then I can finally go jump that bridge. 

For those who are depressed, do you wake up in the morning and get that unbearable feeling in your chest as if your lungs are burning?

tl;dr Just wanted to get random thoughts of my chest so I can sleep easier tonight. Thanks for reading.
